rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address and command to give apply to the whole community of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: هذا الخطاب هو لجميع أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب، عبيدة السلماني، محمد بن سيرين
rows.claim: They take the command as obligatory zakat: do not substitute poor quality for good; voluntary gifts may be small or modest in value.
rows.anchor: فقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وعبيدة السلماني ومحمد بن سيرين: هي في الزكاة المفروضة

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب، الحسن بن أبي الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: They understand the verse as voluntary charity, for which the command recommends rather than obliges giving good-quality goods.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من قول البراء بن عازب والحسن بن أبي الحسن وقتادة، أن الآية في التطوع

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب، عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: They report that Ansar hung date clusters in the mosque for poor emigrants; after a man hung dry, poor dates, the Prophet condemned it and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن الأنصار كانوا أيام الجداد يعلقون أقناء التمر في حبل بين أسطوانتين في المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse covers both obligatory zakat and voluntary charity: the former makes giving good obligatory, the latter makes it recommended.
rows.anchor: والآية تعم الوجهين، لكن صاحب الزكاة يتلقاها على الوجوب وصاحب التطوع يتلقاها على الندب

rows.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
rows.claim: Most interpreters take tayyib as good, choice property and khabith as inferior or base property.
rows.anchor: قالوا معنى من طيبات من جيد ومختار ما كسبتم، وجعلوا الخبيث بمعنى الرديء والرذالة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reads tayyib as lawful earnings and khabith as forbidden property.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد معناه: من حلال ما كسبتم، قال: وقوله: ولا تيمموا الخبيث أي الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd's interpretation is weak in the verse's syntactic sequence, though it is not intrinsically impossible.
rows.anchor: وقول ابن زيد ليس بالقوي من جهة نسق الآية لا من معناه في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayyib may simply mean what you have earned, with its mention praising the quality and blessing of earnings and encompassing both good quality and lawful origin.
rows.anchor: أنفقوا مما كسبتم، فهو حض

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل
rows.claim: He supports the broad reading by saying a believer's property contains nothing vile.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا الاحتمال أن عبد الله بن مغفل قال: ليس في مال المؤمن خبيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earnings include bodily labor and trade, and inheritances count because the human or believing community acquired them.
rows.anchor: وكسبتم معناه كانت لكم فيه سعاية، إما بتعب بدن أو مقاولة في تجارة، والموروث داخل في هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God brings forth from the earth includes plants, minerals, buried treasure, and similar things.
rows.anchor: ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض النباتات والمعادن والركاز وما ضارع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammamu means deliberately to intend or aim at something; two cited poems attest this usage.
rows.anchor: ومنه التيم الذي هو البدل من الوضوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reads tayammamu; al-Bazzi transmits gemination of the initial tā from Ibn Kathir in thirty-one places, beginning here.
rows.anchor: وهكذا قرأ جمهور الناس وروى البزي عن ابن كثير تشديد التاء في أحد وثلاثين موضعا أولها هذا الحرف

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A transmitted reading says la tuʾimmu al-khabīth, using the verb for intending; its meaning matches the standard reading.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري أن في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود «ولا تؤموا الخبيث» من أممت إذا قصدت

rows.speaker: الزهري، مسلم بن جندب
rows.claim: They read the verb with ḍamma on tāʾ and kasra on mīm, following the dialect that says yammamtu for intending.
rows.anchor: وهكذا قرأ جمهور الناس وروى البزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word has forms with light or doubled mīm and with or without the initial tāʾ, all expressing intention.
rows.anchor: وفي اللفظ لغات، منها أممت الشيء خفيفة الميم الأولى وأممته بشدها ويممته وتيممته

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود، أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Another transmitted form is tuʾammamu, with a hamza after tāʾ, reflecting the form with doubled mīm.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو عمرو أن ابن مسعود قرأ «ولا تؤمموا» بهمزة بعد التاء

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: One syntactic analysis ends the sentence at al-khabīth and begins a new description: people spend that vile property though they would accept it only reluctantly.
rows.anchor: قال فريق من الناس: إن الكلام تم في قوله: الخبيث ثم ابتدأ خبرا آخر في وصف الخبيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that analysis, the clause rebukes people, and the pronoun in minhu refers to the vile property.
rows.anchor: كأن هذا المعنى عتاب للناس وتقريع، والضمير في منه عائد على الخبيث

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: A second analysis keeps the syntax connected through fīhi, referring minhu to what was earned and taking tunfiqūn as a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وقال فريق آخر: بل الكلام متصل إلى قوله فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connected construction makes tunfiqūn function as a circumstantial accusative, like saying one goes out only to strive in God's path.
rows.anchor: كأنه في موضع نصب على الحال، وهو كقولك:

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب، ابن عباس، الضحاك
rows.claim: They explain the verse as property owed in debts or rights: one would accept inferior property only by reluctantly waiving part of one's due, so one should not offer God what one dislikes.
rows.anchor: معناه ولستم بآخذيه في ديونكم وحقوقكم عند الناس إلا بأن تساهلوا في ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: He says a buyer would accept such goods in the market only if the seller reduced their price.
rows.anchor: معنى الآية: لستم بآخذيه لو وجدتموه في السوق يباع، إلا أن يهضم لكم من ثمنه

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A similar explanation is transmitted from Ali: one accepts it only after a reduction in its price.
rows.anchor: وروي نحوه عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debt and market-price explanations fit the verse's application to obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: وهذان القولان يشبهان كون الآية في الزكاة الواجبة

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: He also explains the phrase as reluctance to accept an unwanted gift unless one overlooks its poor value, fitting voluntary charity.
rows.anchor: ولستم بآخذيه لو أهدي إليكم إلا أن تغمضوا أي تستحيي من المهدوي أن تقبل منه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the phrase to mean that one would accept forbidden property only by overlooking its repugnance.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد معنى الآية: ولستم بآخذي الحرام إلا أن تغمضوا في مكروهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reads tuġmiḍū with ḍamma on tāʾ, a still ghayn, and kasra on mīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «إلا أن تغمضوا» بضم التاء وسكون الغين وكسر الميم

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri's first reading has fatḥa on tāʾ and a light kasra on mīm; he also transmits a doubled-mīm form with ḍamma on tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري بفتح التاء وكسر الميم مخففا،

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري، مكي
rows.claim: Makkī transmits al-Hasan's form with doubled and open mīm and open tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وحكى مكي عن الحسن البصري «تغمضوا» مشددة الميم

rows.speaker: قتادة، أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Qatada reads with open mīm, and Abu Amr glosses the construction as accepting it only when it is discounted for you.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة بضم التاء وسكون الغين وفتح الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression can derive from a verb meaning to tolerate, waive part of one's due, and accept less than one's full right.
rows.anchor: أغمض الرجل في أمر كذا إذا تساهل فيه ورضي ببعض حقه وتجاوز

rows.speaker: الطرماح بن حكيم
rows.claim: His verse uses al-ighmāḍ for accepting lenient terms and tolerating a shortfall.
rows.anchor: ورضي ببعض حقه وتجاوز، فمن ذلك قول الطرماح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively the word evokes closing one's eyes to something unpleasant, as in another poet's line and the related term al-ighḍāʾ.
rows.anchor: وإما أن تنتزع من تغميض العين لأن الذي يريد الصبر على مكروه يغمض عنه عينيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility derives from going to a remote or obscure place, like the verbs for going to Oman, Iraq, Najd, or the lowlands.
rows.anchor: أغمض الرجل إذا أتى غامضا من الأمر كما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading can mean tolerating, closing one's eyes, or resorting to obscure interpretation when accepting the property, including forbidden, gifted, or owed property under the reported views.
rows.anchor: فقراءة الجمهور تخرج على التجاوز وعلى تغميض العين لأن أغمض بمنزلة غمض

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: He explains al-Zuhri's first reading as reducing the seller's asking price; both al-Zuhri readings can mean taking it at a discount.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة الزهري الأولى فمعناها تهضموا سومها من البائع منكم فيحطكم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dani's account explains al-Zuhri's second reading; Ibn Atiyya also allows that it may refer to closing the eyes.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءته الثانية فهذا مذهب أبي عمرو الداني فيها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr's explanation of Qatada's reading was given above.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة قتادة فقد ذكرت تفسير أبي عمرو لها

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni takes Qatada's form to mean that people are found to have overlooked or interpreted the matter leniently, like finding someone praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: معناها توجدوا قد غمضتم في الأمر بتأولكم أو بتساهلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is self-sufficient and has no need of charity; those seeking closeness and reward should give what is valuable.
rows.anchor: ثم نبه تعالى على صفة الغنى أي لا حاجة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīd means praised in every state and is an essential attribute.
rows.anchor: وحميد معناه محمود في كل حال، وهي صفة ذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses draw people toward charity by exposing Satan's whispering and hostility, recalling God's reward and gift of wisdom, and urging reflection on spending and vows, whether public or hidden.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية وما بعدها وإن لم تكن أمرا بالصدقة فهي جالبة للنفوس إلى الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unrestricted promise normally denotes good, but here the promise is explicitly attached to the unwelcome prospect of poverty; fahshāʾ covers all ugly acts and all sins.
rows.anchor: والوعد في كلام العرب إذا أطلق فهو في الخير وإذا قيد بالموعود ما هو فقد يقيد بالخير وبالشر

rows.speaker: حيوة عن رجل من أهل الرباط
rows.claim: A man from the border garrisons recited al-faqr with ḍamma on the fāʾ, a dialectal form.
rows.anchor: وروى حيوة عن رجل من أهل الرباط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse contains two prompts from Satan and two from God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في الآية اثنتان من الشيطان، واثنتان من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that Satan's prompting threatens evil and denies truth, while the angel's prompting promises truth and confirms good; he recited this verse and advised seeking refuge from Satan's prompting.
rows.anchor: إن للشيطان لمة من ابن آدم وللملك لمة فأما لمة الشيطان فإيعاد بالشر وتكذيب بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness means God's covering of servants in this world and the next; فضل means provision and expansion in this world and bliss in the next, all of which God promises.
rows.anchor: والمغفرة هي الستر على عباده في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash notes an argument that poverty is preferable to wealth because Satan deters people from good by frightening them with poverty.
rows.anchor: ذكر النقاش أن بعض الناس تأنس بهذه الآية في أن الفقر أفضل من الغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is not decisive proof that poverty is superior, although the counterargument is forceful.
rows.anchor: وليس في الآية حجة قاطعة أما إن المعارضة بها قوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Torah report promises that spending from God's provision will bring expanded bounty, and Qur'an 34:39 confirms it.
rows.anchor: فإن يدي مبسوطة على كل يد مبسوطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is واسع because His mercy and knowledge encompass everything.
rows.anchor: وواسع لأنه وسع كل شيء رحمة وعلما

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies wisdom here as prophethood.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي: الحكمة النبوءة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines wisdom as knowledge of the Qur'an, including its abrogating and clear verses, its ambiguous verses, and its Arabic.
rows.anchor: هي المعرفة بالقرآن فقهه ونسخه ومحكمه ومتشابهه وعربيته

rows.speaker: قتادة، مجاهد
rows.claim: They define wisdom as understanding and jurisprudence in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الحكمة الفقه في القرآن، وقاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also defines wisdom as correctness in speech and action.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا: الحكمة الإصابة في القول والفعل

rows.speaker: ابن زيد، زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: They take wisdom as reason or sound judgment in religion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وأبوه زيد بن أسلم: الحكمة العقل في الدين

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik defines wisdom as religious knowledge, understanding, and adherence.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: الحكمة المعرفة في الدين والفقه فيه والاتباع له

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم عن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim transmits Malik's definitions as reflection on God's command and following it, or obedience, religious understanding, and practice.
rows.anchor: وروى عنه ابن القاسم أنه قال: الحكمة التفكر في أمر الله والاتباع له

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi defines wisdom as reverent fear, citing a Prophetic saying that fear of God is the head of everything.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع: الحكمة الخشية، ومنه قول النبي

rows.speaker: إبراهيم، زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Ibrahim and Zayd ibn Aslam define wisdom as understanding.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم: الحكمة الفهم وقاله زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan defines wisdom as scrupulous restraint.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الحكمة الورع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these definitions except al-Suddi's are close: wisdom is mastery or precision in speech and action, and revelation and its applications are parts of that broader quality.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأقوال كلها ما عدا قول السدي قريب بعضها من بعض لأن الحكمة مصدر من الإحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reads the verb passively: whoever is given wisdom; al-Zuhri and Yaqub read it actively, with God as giver and the person as first object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «من يؤت الحكمة» على بناء الفعل للمفعول

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash reads the form with an explicit object pronoun: whoever He gives wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخفش: «ومن يؤته الحكمة»

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym reads, 'You give wisdom to whom You will,' with feminine tāʾ forms, and keeps the next verb in the masculine reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الربيع بن خثيم «تؤتي الحكمة من تشاء» بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's reminder is clear; albāb means intellects, singular lubb.
rows.anchor: وباقي الآية تذكرة بينة وإقامة لهمم الغفلة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، عاصم برواية أبي بكر، ابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers use second-person forms for 'you do' and 'you are denied,' addressing the Muslim community.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم

rows.speaker: حمزة، حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read the verbs in the third person, linking them to the preceding description of those who recite and believe.
rows.anchor: على مشابهة ما تقدم من «يتلون ويؤمنون»

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr used both reading forms.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو يقرأ بالوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takfurohu means the good is given to the doers without them and they receive no reward; a Prophetic saying equates gratitude for a gift with not denying it.
rows.anchor: وتكفروه معناه: يعطى دونكم فلا تثابون عليه

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antarah's verse uses kufr to describe ingratitude by the recipient of a favor.
rows.anchor: والكفر مخبثة لنفس المنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowing the God-fearing is both promise and warning.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: والله عليم بالمتقين وعد ووعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts the righteous with disbelievers; wealth and children are singled out as worldly adornment, the focus of hopes, and people's closest, easiest support.
rows.anchor: وخص الله تعالى «الأموال والأولاد» بالذكر لوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even what disbelievers most pride themselves on cannot avert punishment, so more remote possessions cannot do so either; 'companions of the Fire' implies their lasting state.
rows.anchor: لا غناء فيهما من عقاب الله في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simile pictures disbelievers' supposed devotional spending and its erasure at Judgment as a promising crop destroyed by a scorching wind.
rows.anchor: فوقع التشبيه بين شيئين وشيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison omits one member from each pair and then names the other, an especially eloquent compression; Qur'an 2:171 uses a similar construction.
rows.anchor: وهذه غاية البلاغة والإيجاز، ومثل ذلك قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن هرمز الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads tunfiqūn in the second person, as an instruction to Muhammad to address them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الرحمن بن هرمز الأعرج، «تنفقون» بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority understands spending as wealth spent in pious acts and in hostility to the Messenger, which the disbelievers regarded as devotion.
rows.anchor: وجمهور المفسرين على أن نفقون يراد به الأموال

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the spending refers to their outward statements that conceal the opposite.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: نفقون معناه من أقوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is weak because it makes the passage about hypocrites, whereas its context concerns disbelievers who openly match inward belief and outward conduct.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف، لأنه يقتضي أن الآية في منافقين والآية إنما هي في كفار يعلنون مثل ما يبطنون

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some interpreters take the spending as their deeds, such as disbelief, which nullify other good acts, though the metaphor of spending is strained.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أن نفقون يراد به أعمالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: They define ṣirr as severe, burning cold, also called al-ḍarīb by the Arabs.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وجمهور المفسرين: «الصر» البرد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives ṣirr from making a sound and explains it as the sound of the fire within the wind.
rows.anchor: وذهب الزجاج وغيره: إلى أن اللفظة من التصويت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirr is the fire of Hell in its freezing region, which burns in a way resembling ordinary fire.
rows.anchor: «الصر» هو نفس جهنم الذي في الزمهرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥarth includes crops and fruits, all produced through working the earth; a hadith groups zakatable property as money, produce, or livestock.
rows.anchor: و «الحرث» شامل للزرع والثمار، لأن الجميع

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: They understand the crop owners' wronging themselves as sins against God, making the destruction a fitting and swift punishment.
rows.anchor: ظلم بمعاصي الله، فعلى هذا وقع التشبيه بحرث

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: Some scholars hold that all worldly calamities result from human sins, so any crop destroyed by wind belongs to people who wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: فمن أهل العلم من يرى أن كل مصائب الدنيا فإنما هي بمعاصي العبيد

rows.speaker: المهدوي، بعض الناس
rows.claim: They take 'a people who wronged themselves' to mean farmers sowed outside the proper season.
rows.anchor: معناه زرعوا في غير أوان الزراعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the farmers misplaced their agricultural work in timing or method, which makes the crop especially vulnerable to burning.
rows.anchor: بأن وضعوا أفعال الفلاحة غير موضعها من وقت

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: His verse about a malicious person setting a green palm alight illustrates why destruction of a healthy crop is a fitting comparison.
rows.anchor: وهذا المنزع يشبهه من جهة ما قول امرئ القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'wronged them' refers to the preceding disbelievers, not the crop owners, who were not introduced as people to be reproached; the final clause also points to present wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وليس هو للقوم ذوي الحرث لأنهم لم يذكروا

rows.speaker: السدي وجماعة من المتأولين
rows.claim: They say the verse condemns withholding wealth from God's path, including failure to give obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: الآية نزلت في البخل بالمال والإنفاق في سبيل الله وأداء الزكاة المفروضة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a relative denied a kinsman the surplus he requested, and a bald snake will emerge at Resurrection, lick its lips, and coil around him.
rows.anchor: إلا خرج له يوم القيامة شجاع أقرع من الناس يتلمظ حتى يطوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many sound reports address withholding zakat and hoarding wealth.
rows.anchor: والأحاديث في مثل هذا من منع الزكاة واكتناز المال كثيرة صحيحة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد وجماعة من أهل التفسير
rows.claim: They say the verse concerns People of the Book withholding what they knew about Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الآية إنما نزلت في أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the latter interpretation, yutawwaqūn means they will bear the consequence of what they withheld, from the root for capacity rather than literally being collared.
rows.anchor: فهو من الطاقة كما قال تعالى: وعلى الذين يطيقونه

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai says they will be given a collar of fire at Resurrection, consistent with the wealth interpretation.
rows.anchor: سيطوقون سيجعل لهم يوم القيامة طوق من نار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they will be charged to produce the like of what they withheld, fitting the interpretation about withheld knowledge.
rows.anchor: سيكلفون أن يأتوا بمثل ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With yaḥsabanna read in the third person, alladhīna yabkhalūn is the subject; an omitted first object is 'their stinginess,' khayran is the second object, and huwa is a separator.
rows.anchor: وإعراب قوله تعالى: الذين يبخلون رفع في قراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The understood noun 'stinginess' is supplied by the verb 'they are stingy,' like the poet's use of 'foolish' to imply foolishness.
rows.anchor: ودل قوله: يبخلون على هذا البخل المقدر كما

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The verse cited in the wāfir meter shows how an adjective such as 'foolish' implies the abstract quality of folly.
rows.anchor: إذ نهي السفيه جرى إليه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: With taḥsabanna addressed to Muhammad, an omitted genitive is understood: do not consider the stinginess of those who are stingy good for them; it is like 'ask the town.'
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: وهي مثل وسئل القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the heavens and earth God's inheritance speaks in human terms of everything perishing and God alone remaining its owner, though His ownership is eternal.
rows.anchor: ولله ميراث السماوات خطاب على ما يفعله البشر دال على فناء الجميع وأنه لا يبقى مالك إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read 'God knows what they do' with third-person yāʾ, referring to those who are stingy and collared.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو «والله بما يعملون» بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use second-person tāʾ, shifting from absent to addressed listeners after the preceding address in 3:179.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتاء من فوق، وذلك على الرجوع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the statement that God is poor arose when Abu Bakr visited a Jewish study house and confronted the scholar Finhas; after Finhas mocked the idea of God's loan, Abu Bakr struck him, and the Prophet questioned Abu Bakr before the verse came down.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت بسبب فنحاص اليهودي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the verse concerns Huyayy ibn Akhtab's mockery of the Qur'anic invitation to lend God a good loan.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: نزلت الآية في حيي بن أخطب

rows.speaker: الحسن، معمر، قتادة
rows.claim: They say Jews broadly mocked the loan verse, arguing that only a poor person borrows from a rich one.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن ومعمر وقتادة أيضا وغيرهم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt likely began with Finhas, Huyayy, and similar scholars, then spread among Jews; it misleads followers through wordplay and distorts scripture.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza alone reads the recording passively, makes 'the killing of the prophets' nominative, and reads 'it will be said' in the third person.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحده «سيكتب» بالياء من أسفل على بناء الفعل للمفعول

rows.speaker: باقي القراء
rows.claim: The other readers use the first-person plural for writing and saying, with 'their killing' accusative as an object or coordinated phrase.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بنون الجمع، فإما أنها نون العظمة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود، أبو معاذ
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reading has 'it will be said: taste'; Abu Muadh transmits 'we will write what they say, and it will be said to them: taste.'
rows.anchor: وقال أبو معاذ النحوي في حرف ابن مسعود: «سنكتب ما يقولون ويقال لهم ذوقوا»

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف، أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Talha reads 'we will write what they say'; Abu Amr also transmits a passive form meaning their statement will be written.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «سنكتب ما يقولون» وحكى أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings convey nearly the same threat: their sayings and deeds will be recorded, alongside their fathers' killing of prophets; fathers and children share pronouns because children follow and approve their fathers.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية وعيد لهم، أي سيحصى عليهم قولهم

rows.speaker: كثير من العلماء
rows.claim: Many scholars take the writing literally: angels record deeds on tablets, and God creates their weight or lightness for weighing.
rows.anchor: والكتب فيما قال كثير من العلماء هو في صحف تقيده الملائكة فيها

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others take writing as an idiom for complete accounting and lack of neglect, which is the verse's meaning.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن الكتب عبارة عن الإحصاء وعدم الإهمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Taste' metaphorically means direct experience, since taste is a particularly acute and discriminating sense; ḥarīq means burning or may name a level of Hell.
rows.anchor: والذوق مع العذاب مستعار، عبارة عن المباشرة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري، ابن زيد وجماعة
rows.claim: They say the verse concerns hypocrites who stayed behind on campaigns, offered excuses, and wanted praise as would-be fighters whom circumstances had detained.
rows.anchor: الآية نزلت في المنافقين، وذلك أنهم كانوا إذا خرج النبي

rows.speaker: جماعة كثيرة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Many interpreters say the verse concerns Jewish scholars, though they differ over what the Jews did and what praise they wanted.
rows.anchor: وقالت جماعة كثيرة من المفسرين إنما نزلت الآية في أهل الكتاب أحبار اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One account says Jewish scholars rejoiced at leading their followers away from belief in Muhammad to preserve their worldly leadership, while wanting praise as scriptural scholars.
rows.anchor: أتوا إضلال أتباعهم عن الإيمان بمحمد وفرحوا بذلك لدوام رياستهم الدنيوية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك، السدي
rows.claim: They say the Jews agreed and exchanged letters across regions to deny Muhammad and block his mission, while claiming praise for prayer, fasting, and worship.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا والضحاك والسدي: أتوا أنهم تعاقدوا وتكاتبوا من كل قطر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they rejoiced that followers admired their altered interpretation of the Torah and wanted praise, despite doing nothing useful or true.
rows.anchor: فرحوا بإعجاب أتباعهم بتبديلهم تأويل التوراة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He says the Jews rejoiced at God's giving Abraham's family prophethood and scripture, claiming to follow them and wanting praise despite not following their way; his reading ūtu means 'were given.'
rows.anchor: فرحوا بما أعطى الله آل إبراهيم من النبوءة والكتاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says people concealed the truth when the Prophet questioned them, gave him a false answer, and rejoiced while expecting praise and believing he accepted it.
rows.anchor: إن الآية نزلت في قوم سألهم النبي عليه السلام عن شيء فكتموه الحق وقالوا له غير ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Jews of Khaybar feigned agreement with the Prophet and Muslims while inwardly opposing them, then wanted praise for their public stance.
rows.anchor: نافقوا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين مرة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj describes Jews who told Muslims after meeting the Prophet that he had told them familiar things, gaining praise and hopes of conversion while hiding their opposition.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية في قوم من اليهود

rows.speaker: أبو المكارم
rows.claim: Abu al-Makarem explains the word mafaza as a place crossed by whoever succeeds in passing through it.
rows.anchor: قال لي أبو المكارم: إنما سميت «مفازة» لأن من قطعها فاز

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says a bitten person is called salim as an expression of optimism.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: سمي اللديغ سليما تفاؤلا

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says the bitten person is called salim because he has surrendered to what happened to him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: بل لأنه مستسلم لما أصابه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some interpreters read God ownership of the heavens and earth as a response to the claim that God was poor and people rich.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: الآية رد على الذين قالوا

rows.speaker: القاضي ابن الطيب وآخرون
rows.claim: They say God power over everything appears universal but is limited in Arabic usage because impossible things are not objects of divine power.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي ابن الطيب وغيره: ظاهره العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and creatures provide evidence for a Creator and for knowledge; an existing knower and willing agent cannot be lifeless.
rows.anchor: ثم دل على مواضع النظر والعبرة، حيث يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day alternate and differ in length as well as in light and darkness; ayat means signs.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الليل والنهار هو تعاقبهما، إذ جعلهما الله خلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of understanding are intellects shaped by religious obligation rather than mere experience.
rows.anchor: والألباب في هذه الآية: هي ألباب التكليف لا ألباب التجربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innāmā can express true logical restriction or rhetorical emphasis, as in 'God is one' and the eulogy 'the brave is Antarah'; the verse calls for examining its restrictive wording.
rows.anchor: إنما حاصرة، وهو مقصد المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage repentance is returning from evil to good; its defining element is regret for a past act because it disobeyed God, not because it harmed one's body or property.
rows.anchor: وحد التوبة: الندم على فارط فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the sinner can repeat the act, sincere repentance also requires resolve not to repeat it; an act that can no longer be repeated needs no such condition.
rows.anchor: فمن شروط التوبة العزم على ترك ذلك الفعل في المستأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is obligatory by communal consensus, which supports reading the command in Qur'an 24:31 as an obligation.
rows.anchor: والتوبة فرض على المؤمنين بإجماع الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may repent of one sin while persisting in a different kind of sin, contrary to the Muʿtazila; later relapse does not invalidate a completed earlier repentance but requires a new one.
rows.anchor: وتصح التوبة من ذنب من الإقامة على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A disbeliever's faith is not itself repentance; repentance is regret for the prior disbelief.
rows.anchor: والإيمان للكافر ليس نفس توبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Upon God' omits a noun meaning God's bounty and mercy, as in the hadith about God's and servants' rights, which means God's gracious favor rather than a rational debt.
rows.anchor: على الله فيه حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing is rationally incumbent on God, but what God says He has made incumbent becomes binding by revelation; this includes punishment of unbelief and accepting faith, while acceptance of repentance is not rationally required.
rows.anchor: والعقيدة: أنه لا يجب على الله تعالى شيء عقلا

rows.speaker: أبو المعالي وآخرون
rows.claim: They say scriptural promises of accepting repentance provide a strong presumption, not certainty, that God will accept it.
rows.anchor: فهذه الظواهر إنما تعطي غلبة ظن لا قطعا

rows.speaker: أبو المعالي وآخرون
rows.claim: Al-Maali's view is opposed by those who hold that a person meeting every condition of sincere repentance is certainly accepted.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرضنا رجلا قد تاب توبة نصوحا تامة الشروط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya's father favored certainty of acceptance, and Ibn Atiyya adopts it because God says He accepts repentance and forgives those who repent and believe.
rows.anchor: وكان أبي رحمة الله عليه يميل إلى هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sūʾ includes disbelief and sins; bi-jahāla means folly and poor judgment leading to sin, not ignorance that the act is sinful.
rows.anchor: والسوء في هذه الآية يعم الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: قتادة، ابن عباس، مجاهد، السدي
rows.claim: Qatada says the Companions agreed every sin is committed in ignorance, whether deliberate or inadvertent; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Suddi also support this explanation.
rows.anchor: اجتمع أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على أن كل معصية

rows.speaker: مجاهد، الضحاك
rows.claim: They also explain 'in ignorance' here as acting deliberately.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد والضحاك أنهما قالا:

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the affairs of worldly life are all called ignorance; Ibn Atiyya restricts this to worldly pursuits outside obedience and links it to Qur'an 47:36 and 57:20.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: أمور الدنيا كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that 'ignorance' simply means worldly life is weak; the further claim that it means not knowing the full punishment is also weak and was rejected by Ibn Furak.
rows.anchor: وهذا عندي ضعيف، وقيل بجهالة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي
rows.claim: They define 'before long' as before illness and death.
rows.anchor: فابن عباس رضي الله عنه ذكر أحسن أوقات التوبة

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز، محمد بن قيس، الضحاك، عكرمة، ابن زيد وآخرون
rows.claim: They define 'before long' as before the angels become visible, death seizes the person, and self-command is lost.
rows.anchor: والجمهور حددوا آخر وقتها

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة
rows.claim: Abu Qilaba relates that Iblis vowed to tempt Adam's descendants while their spirits remain, and God vowed not to bar repentance while they remain alive.
rows.anchor: وعزتي لا أحجب عنه التوبة ما دام فيه الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas names repentance's best time, while the majority identify its latest limit.
rows.anchor: فابن عباس رضي الله عنه ذكر أحسن أوقات التوبة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai transmits the maxim that repentance remains open until the soul is seized at the throat.
rows.anchor: كان يقال: التوبة مبسوطة لأحدكم

rows.speaker: بشير بن كعب، الحسن، النبي
rows.claim: They transmit a Prophetic report that God accepts a servant's repentance until the death rattle and loss of reason.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that stage repentance is impossible because the person can no longer regret the act or resolve to stop it; 'near' means near the sin, and repentance while healthy is better than delay.
rows.anchor: فإذا غلب تعذرت التوبة لعدم الندم والعزم على الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All of life is still near in relation to the sin, while death is the farthest point; Ibn Atiyya cites Malik ibn al-Rayb's verse about distance.
rows.anchor: ومدة الحياة كلها قريب، والمبادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who repents and guides them to repentance; His wisdom also governs the delay by which others are destroyed.
rows.anchor: أي بمن يتوب وييسره هو للتوبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن زيد وجماعة المفسرين
rows.claim: They say the excluded person is one whose death has arrived and who has entered despair, like Pharaoh during drowning.
rows.anchor: وحضور الموت هو غاية قربه

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi says the first verse addresses believers and the second originally addressed Muslims, then was abrogated by Qur'an 4:48 and 4:116, which denies forgiveness for associating partners and leaves other believers to God's will.
rows.anchor: والآية الثانية قوله: وليست التوبة الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abrogation claim is weak: although phrased as a report, the verse establishes a legal ruling, and no abrogation is needed because it excludes only repentance at death, not forgiveness for an unrepentant sinner under Qur'an 4:48 and 4:116.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه الآية لم تنف أن يغفر للعاصي الذي لم يتب من قريب

rows.speaker: أبو المعالي وآخرون
rows.claim: A repentant person who turns back before death has the status of the repentant; al-Maali says the scriptural promise makes salvation likely, while others say forgiveness is certain.
rows.anchor: العقيدة عندي في هذه الآيات:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who waits until death is not treated as repentant: an unbeliever remains eternally in punishment, while a sinful believer is under God's will, with fear of punishment prevailing though some are certainly forgiven by grace.
rows.anchor: فإن كان كافرا فهو يخلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If 'those' refers only to dying unbelievers, their punishment is eternal; if it includes sinners who delay repentance until death, their punishment is not eternal.
rows.anchor: وأعلم الله تعالى أيضا أن الذين يموتون وهم كفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿtadnā means prepared and made present; the verse's wording indicates that Hell already exists.
rows.anchor: وظاهر هذه الآية أن النار مخلوقة بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people addressed were poor, socially weak believers, including Bilal, Ammar, Ibn Umm Abd, Murthid al-Ghanawi, Khabbab, Suhayb, Subayh, Dhul-Shimalayn, and al-Miqdad.
rows.anchor: المراد ب الذين ضعفة المؤمنين في ذلك الوقت في أمور الدنيا بلال وعمار وابن أم عبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some unbelievers said their status and rank prevented them from mixing with the poor; if Muhammad expelled them, the elites would follow him. A report also attributes the advice to Abu Talib, and Quraysh leaders gathered to press it; the author thinks the proposal was likely a ruse.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: نحن لشرفنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says some unbelievers asked to move the poor believers out of the front prayer row so they could take their places and believe.
rows.anchor: إن بعض الكفار إنما طلب أن يؤخر هؤلاء عن الصف الأول في الصلاة

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت عن الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits that al-Aqraʿ ibn Habis and similar Arab notables asked for a separate meeting without slaves or allies and for a written agreement; Muhammad considered it before the verse came down.
rows.anchor: أسند الطبري إلى خباب بن الأرت أن الأقرع بن حابس ومن شابهه من أشراف العرب قالوا للنبي

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi says all the pronouns in the passage refer to the believers; Hasan says their accounting concerns their deeds, as most interpreters hold.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا تجيء الضمائر كلها للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first min is partitive and the second is emphatic; the two fa-verbs follow the prior negation and prohibition, and being among wrongdoers means putting things in the wrong place.
rows.anchor: ومن الأولى للتبعيض والثانية زائدة مؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitannā means tested: believers are tested by harm from unbelievers, and unbelievers by seeing socially low people honored and given rank by this religion and the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فتنا معناه في هذه الآية: ابتلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the lām in li-yaqūlū as a result of God's decree, as in Qur'an 28:8, so the unbelievers mock the weak believers' favor.
rows.anchor: فهي لام الصيرورة كما قال تعالى: فالتقطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading takes the lām as purpose: the elites question this favor among themselves, and their discussion may guide some of them.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل الكلام معنى آخر وهو أن تكون اللام في ليقولوا على بابها في لام كي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading is more immediate, though the second is possible; on either reading, 'favored' reflects the believers' understanding of God's favor.
rows.anchor: والتأويل الأول أسبق والثاني يتخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows best who is grateful for His favor and where it should be placed; the rhetorical question states an obvious truth that the mockers cannot contest.
rows.anchor: فالله أعلم بمن يشكر نعمته والمواضع التي ينبغي أن يوضع فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wazn is a verbal noun; the verse can be parsed with 'the weight' as subject and 'the truth' as predicate, or 'that day' as predicate and 'true' as an adjective: true weighing is established or manifest on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: الوزن مصدر وزن يزن، ورفعه بالابتداء

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group takes scales and weighing as a metaphor for the meticulous justice of Judgment, using the familiar image of a balance; Abu Talib's verse illustrates this sense.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يعلم عباده أن الحساب والنظر يوم القيامة هو في غاية التحرير ونهاية العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the metaphorical view is weaker: Qur'anic wording and a Prophetic report direct a person to seek the Prophet at the visible balance, weighing poses no problem, and abandoning the literal sense without cause risks denying revealed realities.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أصح من الأول من جهات

rows.speaker: مجاهد، الضحاك
rows.claim: This metaphorical view is also reported from Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others, who understand heaviness and lightness as the abundance or scarcity of good deeds.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا القول عن مجاهد والضحاك وغيره

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority say the Judgment balance has a beam and two pans like worldly balances, displaying exact justice through a familiar object.
rows.anchor: وقال جمهور الأمة: إن الله عز وجل أراد أن يعرض

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: Hudhayfa says Gabriel is the custodian of the balances on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قال حذيفة بن اليمان رضي الله عنه: صاحب الموازين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance should be understood literally; reports say records of good and bad deeds go into its pans, where God creates heaviness or lightness.
rows.anchor: فإن الآثار تظاهرت بأن صحائف الحسنات والسيئات توضع في كفتي الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weight must occur in a body, since an accident cannot inhere in another accident; it may occur in the records or nearby bodies, and Abu al-Maali favors the records.
rows.anchor: ولا بد لنا أن نعلم أن الثقل الحادث مع الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unreliable reports about the balance's shape and length need not be repeated; Hasan's report that each person has a separate balance is rejected because the balance is one, though each person has an individual weighing.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن فيما روي عنه:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the 'scales' are the good deeds themselves; Ibn Atiyya says the plural highlights the many weighed acts.
rows.anchor: ثقلت موازينه أن «الموازين» الحسنات نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mufliḥūn are those who attain what they seek and succeed; the cited poem uses aflaḥa for attainment, while another verse may use falāḥ for survival, which is closely related.
rows.anchor: والمفلحون في اللغة المدركون لبغيتهم الناجحون في طلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's weighing, recording deeds, and making limbs testify despite His knowledge serve to establish proof; the testimony of divine oneness must tip a person's balance.
rows.anchor: فقد تقرر في الشرع أن كلمة التوحيد ترجح ميزان من وزنت في أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author asks how sinful believers can have a weighty balance and be judged successful yet still enter Hell.
rows.anchor: كيف تثقل موازين العصاة من المؤمنين بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A light balance means the pan of good deeds rises; they lose themselves through destruction and eternal residence in Hell.
rows.anchor: المعنى من خفت كفة حسناته فشالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-mā expresses recompense, like thanking someone for what they did; mā is a verbal noun, and God's signs are proofs, commands, and prohibitions that they wrong by disbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: بما كانوا أي جزاء بذلك كما تقول أكرمتك

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: One answer is that good deeds are weighed without tawhid first, then tawhid makes the balance heavy when sinful believers are released from Hell.
rows.anchor: فقالت طائفة إنه توزن أعمالهم دون التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that a sinner will not remain forever in Hell counts as success, even if disciplinary punishment comes first.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فمعرفة العاصي أنه غير مخلد فلاح

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: One answer is that good deeds are weighed without tawhid first, then tawhid makes the balance heavy when sinful believers are released from Hell.
rows.anchor: فقالت طائفة إنه توزن أعمالهم دون التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that a sinner will not remain forever in Hell counts as success, even if disciplinary punishment comes first.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فمعرفة العاصي أنه غير مخلد فلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rejecting the unbelievers' own claims about forbidden things, the verse states what God has actually prohibited.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم إنكار ما حرمه الكفار بآرائهم، أتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawāḥish are foul and ugly things; the term began with ugliness in appearance and expanded to ugly conduct, coarse language, and indecency, as poetry and reports illustrate.
rows.anchor: والفواحش ما فحش وشنع وأصله من القبح في المنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moral good and evil are known through revelation; anything the law prohibits is a fahisha even if reason does not independently condemn it, such as men wearing silk or gold.
rows.anchor: والقبح والحسن في المعاني إنما يتلقى من جهة الشرع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives naked circumambulation as manifest indecency and fornication as hidden indecency; these are examples of the comprehensive division.
rows.anchor: قال ما ظهر الطواف عريانا، والبواطن الزنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'what is manifest and hidden' covers the whole category; mā is partitive apposition from fawāḥish, with the two parts together representing the whole.
rows.anchor: ما ظهر منها وما بطن يجمع النوع كله

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand ithm broadly as every act or statement that incurs sin.
rows.anchor: والإثم أيضا: لفظه عام لجميع الأفعال والأقوال

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some identify ithm as wine and cite a poem about drinking sin until one's reason flew away.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: هي الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wine interpretation is wrong because the surah is Meccan and wine was not prohibited until Medina after Uhud, when some Companions drank it and died as martyrs with it in their bodies; the poem may be fabricated or elliptical.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مردود لأن هذه السورة مكية ولم تعن الشريعة لتحريم الخمر إلا بالمدينة بعد أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a surface reading of Qur'an 2:219 might suggest wine is a sin and therefore prohibited, 'sin in them' can mean harmful acts caused by wine; Companions still drank after that verse, and wine was prohibited later by Qur'an, hadith, and consensus.
rows.anchor: ولكن لا يصح هذا لأن قوله فيهما إثم لفظ محتمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghy means exceeding the limit, even when retaliating; 'without right' clarifies the point because aggression cannot truly be just.
rows.anchor: والبغي: التعدي وتجاوز الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on associating partners concerns idols and everything worshipped besides God; sulṭān means proof, and speaking about God without knowledge includes inventing bans such as those on bahīra and sāʾiba.
rows.anchor: وأن تشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا المراد بها الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community or group has a fixed term for punishment when it disbelieves or disobeys; the warning applies to Muhammad's community as well.
rows.anchor: أجل مؤقت لمجيء العذاب إذا كفروا

rows.speaker: الحسن، ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin read the word for terms in the plural; Abu al-Fath says plural is more apparent because every person has a term, while the singular is a collective genus.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «فإذا جاء آجالهم» بالجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāʿa names the smallest piece of time but stands for every part of time, as 'not even an atom's weight' does in Qur'an 4:40.
rows.anchor: ساعة لفظ عين به الجزء القليل من الزمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent conflict with promises to delay punishment if people believe in Qur'an 14:10 and 71:4 is resolved by the Sunni view that each person has one fixed term: those destined to disbelieve meet it sooner, while believers reach their appointed later term.
rows.anchor: والحق مذهب أهل السنة أن كل أحد إنما هو بأجل واحد لا يتأخر عنه ولا يتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah did not know which people belonged to either group, so he called everyone to salvation; Muhammad likewise calls all people to Paradise while knowing some will disbelieve, like a prisoner offered conversion or death.
rows.anchor: وغيب عن نوح تعيين الطائفتين فندب الكل إلى طريق النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to Adam's children applies to all humanity; inna with mā is emphatic and permits the emphatic nūn, while the verb is future to keep the coming of messengers in view at revelation and attest Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: الخطاب في هذه الآية لجميع العالم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب، الأعرج
rows.claim: They read taʾtiyannakum in agreement with the plural 'messengers,' then use the masculine plural 'they recount' according to the meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب والأعرج «تأتينكم» على لفظ الرسل

rows.speaker: أبو سيار السلمي عن الطبري
rows.claim: Abu Sayyar reports that God gathered Adam and his descendants, addressed them with the coming-messengers passage, then addressed the messengers with Qur'an 23:51-52 before dispersing them.
rows.anchor: أسند الطبري إلى أبي سيار السلمي قال إن الله تعالى جعل آدم وذريته في كفه
